questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In 1925, Nana's grandma wrote a letter by hand to a friend. Today, Nana sends her friend an email. What purpose do both texts share?
choices: To share news with a friend
To sell something to a stranger
questions.explanation: Both the old letter and the new email are written to share news with someone the writer knows.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An old newspaper advertisement from 1930 and a new online advertisement both sell biscuits. What is the same about them?
choices: They both use exactly the same words
They both try to make people want to buy the biscuits
They both are printed on paper
questions.explanation: Advertisements from any time have the same purpose: to persuade people to buy something.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence comes from a persuasive text?
choices: Once, a koala named Kip lost his last gum leaf.
Every school should plant a vegetable garden, because fresh food keeps kids healthy.
First, mix the flour and the eggs in a bowl.
A kangaroo can bound up to 9 metres in one hop.
questions.explanation: The writer gives an opinion ('should') and a reason to convince the reader.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mia writes an informative report about the Great Barrier Reef. Which feature will help readers find facts quickly?
questions.explanation: Headings show what each part is about, so readers can find facts fast.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A story begins: 'The old gum tree whispered a secret to Jess.' What makes this sentence imaginative?
choices: The tree is given a human action
It gives a true fact about gum trees
It tells the reader how to plant a tree
It asks the reader to vote
questions.explanation: Trees cannot whisper. Giving a tree a human action is a feature of imaginative writing.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Tom packs his togs, towel and sunscreen. He runs to the car and calls, 'Hurry, Dad! The waves are perfect today!' Where is Tom most likely going?
questions.explanation: Togs, towel, sunscreen and waves are clues that point to the beach.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Read this. 'Echidnas are small mammals with spikes on their backs. When in danger, they curl into a ball or dig down into the soil.' Which is the best summary?
choices: Echidnas dig soil because it is fun.
Echidnas have spikes and stay safe by curling up or digging.
Echidnas live in Australia and eat ants.
questions.explanation: A summary gives the main ideas. The other choices add things the text does not say.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Sam reads: 'The wind howled and the tin roof rattled all night.' What should Sam picture?
choices: A sunny afternoon at the beach
A stormy night with loud noises
questions.explanation: Howled and rattled are noisy words, so the picture is a windy, stormy night.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which long word is split into syllables correctly?
questions.explanation: Fantastic has three beats: fan-tas-tic. Each beat has one vowel sound.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word is in the same word family as 'signal'?
questions.explanation: Signal and signature both come from the same old word for 'sign' or 'mark'.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The children left ___ hats on the bench. Which word fits the sentence?
questions.explanation: 'Their' shows the hats belong to the children.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The words 'weather' and 'whether' sound the same but have different meanings.
questions.explanation: Words that sound the same but mean different things are called homophones.
